event.detail:
# Old pages misdraw reattachments after the protocol-77 update

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

A browser page left open across this update can briefly reconnect with its old renderer, show grid messages as terminal output, and lose the attachment when the user types. Reloading restores the terminal. This behavior is explicitly accepted by the changed specification, so this is a proposed drop rather than a reported defect.

## Details

Source basis: assigned patch lines 227-238, SPEC_impl.md at the reviewed revision, Grid streams. Exact acceptance: "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working." It then states "any reconnect from it, automatic in that window or manual, misdraws the terminal" and "what is typed into it ends the attachment as malformed input." Exact decision: "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy."

Contract: protocol skew refuses incompatible helm/supervisor pairs, but this page/helm compatibility is intentionally not preserved. Suggested bucket: high/material UX if it were not accepted. Confidence: confirmed as a specification decision; no runtime behavior observed. proposed_drop: explicit quoted specification acceptance. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; malformed input is specified to end the attachment rather than reach the program. No claim that this preserves unsent typing or existing selection.

## Details

Revision of c1 after source validation; original consequence retained. Source basis: assigned patch lines 227-238, SPEC_impl.md:3021-3027, Grid streams. Exact acceptance: "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working." It then states "any reconnect from it, automatic in that window or manual, misdraws the terminal" and "what is typed into it ends the attachment as malformed input." Exact decision: "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy."

Checks actually made: the preceding revision's terminal.js:4651-4667 builds xterm for unknown kind; :5719-5725 treats unannounced data as bytes; :5886-5924 treats a missing notice as bytes and refuses that if a direct grid already exists. The reviewed revision's terminal.rs:750-800 forwards binary input as grid messages and ignores old pause/resume controls; service/grid_stream.rs:1064-1079 decodes GridInput before producing any program bytes. Protocol source lib.rs:255 sets version 77, and io.rs:585-653 accepts only exact protocol matches, preventing old supervisor byte streams from entering a new helm. The page/helm transition is separate from that peer handshake.

Material caveat: the specification's word "any" overstates the misdraw path. An old page retaining a known host kind builds its grid directly and refuses missing stream notice instead; the misdraw requires the kind to be unknown, as the paragraph's explanation describes after the new listing. Both paths break attachment and have the same prescribed reload remedy; no additional material consequence from that wording difference was established. No runtime behavior was observed.

Contract: old-page compatibility across this update is intentionally not preserved. Suggested bucket: high/material UX if it were not accepted. Confidence: confirmed from source and the explicit specification decision. proposed_drop: explicit quoted specification acceptance; the known-kind caveat does not establish a separate user-facing defect. possible_cover: none searched. event.detail:
# Check valid-JSON old-page paste reinterpretation

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

The parent supplied a distinct route beyond the ordinary old-page misdraw/detach already considered: a paste that is valid grid-input JSON may be accepted as structured input, changing the pasted text into program control characters. This could execute unintended commands rather than merely end an attachment. The route needs direct source validation in this group.

## Details

Revision of original c1 to lead, preserving its original consequence and proposed-drop basis without accepting that drop. Original established concern: an old browser page reconnecting across protocol 77 can misdraw grid output or refuse the missing stream notice; malformed raw input ends its attachment. Exact prior proposed_drop basis in SPEC_impl.md:3021-3027: "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working." The paragraph specifies "what is typed into it ends the attachment as malformed input" and "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy." No parent drop has been accepted.

New parent-supplied cross-group input: g196/l1:10 reports that a fresh unknown-kind old page mounts xterm with bracketed paste initially off, its paste path can emit a whole literal-JSON onData frame, and the current GridInput::Text decoder unescapes data and sends controls without bracketed-paste protection. That would not be refuted by a decoder rejecting malformed input. g196 is checking global build-skew mount/paste interlocks. These are supplied source claims, not yet validated here and not execution evidence.

Suggested bucket: potentially highest/security or loss of work if a shipped user paste is transformed into commands by an unbracketed carriage return; established previous misdraw/detach remains high/material UX if unaccepted. Could-be-highest: yes, the newly supplied valid-message route needs investigation. Confidence: uninvestigated lead, not a completed finding. proposed_drop: earlier exact reload acceptance remains recorded for ordinary misdraw/malformed detach only; whether it accepts successful command reinterpretation must be independently assessed. possible_cover: g196/l1 supplied by parent, not a coverage search. Next checks: read supplied latest neighbour record, trace the preceding page's paste/frame production and build-skew guards, current message decode/encoder, and pinned contracts; establish the literal-JSON-to-control route and its limits without runtime reproduction.

event.summary: An old page can turn a literal JSON paste into unbracketed terminal commands
event.detail:
# An old page can turn a literal JSON paste into terminal commands

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

A page left open through the grid-only update can interpret a pasted JSON document as a terminal-input instruction. Instead of inserting that document literally, it sends the document's data field to the program; JSON escapes for carriage return become real unbracketed Enter input. In a shell tab this can run commands the user intended only to paste as document text.

## Details

Discovery-turn revision of original c1 from lead to finding, preserving its original old-page misdrawing, missing-notice refusal and ordinary malformed-input detachment consequences and prior proposed-drop basis. The new successful-input route supersedes c1's earlier broad no-highest conclusion. No parent drop or lowering has been accepted.

Source validated directly this turn: the preceding page's terminal.js:2650-2675 dispatches text clipboard content through insert; :2232-2235 sanitizes only through term-bytes.js:55-56 (removes literal ESC/end markers, not JSON backslash escapes). Its installed callback at :4628-4634 calls term.paste. The preceding vendor/xterm.js:1 paste routine converts literal CRLF/LF, adds markers only when its own decPrivateModes.bracketedPasteMode is true, and calls triggerDataEvent once with the whole prepared text. Its default modes set bracketedPasteMode:false. Parent terminal.js:4191-4196 sends that onData result through sendData at :4157-4158 as one UTF-8 WebSocket binary message. The reviewed helm's terminal.rs:762-773 forwards that message unchanged as one grid input frame. farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:1565-1566 uses serde's internally tagged t field, :1610-1612 defines Text { data }, :1650-1655 parses JSON, and :1686-1693 validates Text length without rejecting decoded control characters. grid_input.rs:175 encodes Text.data as its raw bytes, outside paste wrapping regardless of the real program's bracketed-paste mode. service/grid_stream.rs:1064-1090 decodes, encodes and queues that accepted message. Thus a small one-line pasted JSON Text document can be reinterpreted into actual control-bearing program input. The earlier malformed-input check does not refute a valid input document.

Caller prerequisites: earlier direct checks established unknown-kind mounting and missing-notice byte interpretation at parent terminal.js:4651-4667,5719-5725,5886-5924. Parent-supplied latest g088/l2 separately confirms missing agent_terminal/tab.kind defaults, a live ordinary session's terminal admission, fresh mount despite build skew, and no modal/input veto from BuildSkewNotice. Parent-supplied g196/l1 and g082/c2 identify this same full paste route, not an independent new discovery. My prior direct reconnect checks confirm automatic retries stop once mismatch is observed but manual attachment remains; that gate does not reject raw binary paste on an already open socket. New hello protocol 77 excludes older supervisors, not the old browser page.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:3021-3027 explicitly describes old pages misdrawing and says "what is typed into it ends the attachment as malformed input." Successful interpretation of document contents as control input is a distinct consequence. The product's deliberate user-paste delivery does not make JSON decoding part of the user's intended literal paste. Suggested fix direction: preserve compatible page negotiation or reject incompatible browser input before routing, so raw legacy bytes cannot masquerade as grid messages. No implementation change is requested or made by this review.

Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of work, for an established conditional route from literal paste to unbracketed commands; no particular destructive command or loss was observed. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: likely, naming runtime trigger conditions: a fresh unknown-kind legacy xterm surface remains attached until a small valid-Text-JSON paste, with no misparsed output having enabled that surface's initially-off bracketed-paste mode. The source shows the necessary code paths and defaults; occurrence and frequency were not executed. No readily checkable source premise remains missing for this conditional route.

proposed_drop: false for successful input reinterpretation. Preserve the exact prior proposed drop for ordinary display/malformed-input failure: "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working" and "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy." Whether that general reload acceptance also accepts successful command reinterpretation requires independent judgment; it cannot be treated as a source refutation. possible_cover: parent-supplied g196/l1, g082/c2, g083/c5 and g088/l2 for consolidation; no coverage-source search. Caveats: known-host direct-grid old mounts instead refuse missing notice; ordinary keystrokes generally fail decoding; an old renderer with bracketed paste already enabled would not send this particular valid-JSON raw frame. All evidence is source and contract analysis. No runtime test, reproduction, build or live-install action was performed.

# Removing the xterm OSC scheme filter retains the page allowlist

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether removing the old renderer's OSC hyperlink filter would let terminal output open arbitrary local URL handlers. The replacement keeps an explicit http/https/file boundary before activation; no bypass was established.

## Details

The changed SPEC_impl.md Session-host file reads paragraph (lines 3656-3658) says the grid passes all OSC 8 targets to the page and assigns the boundary to oscTarget. SPEC.md Terminal experience requires: "OSC hyperlink schemes are explicitly limited to http, https and file; every other scheme is ignored."

Source checks at the reviewed commit: crates/farhelm-ui/assets/terminal-files.js:128-148 oscTarget accepts parsed http/https, then only a validated absolute file URI with no control characters, query or fragment. crates/farhelm-ui/assets/terminal.js:1025-1064 oscLink dispatches only target.kind web/file; its remaining branch installs inert hover and activate callbacks. createGridLinks:1105-1112 wraps every OSC row link with oscLink before returning the provider result. Thus removing the xterm-specific allowNonHttpProtocols discussion does not remove the page boundary. Printed links retain their separate existing web activation checks.

Suggested bucket: highest/security if arbitrary local scheme execution were reachable; that route is refuted here. Could-be-highest: yes, this was a security-boundary candidate, but source has no shipped activation path for other schemes. Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation through the explicit allowlist and inert fallback above. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: this check covers the removed renderer boundary and its replacement, not unrelated URL parser behavior or the entire link subsystem.

Synthesis checked the caller and overlapping-provider assumptions. crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-buffer.js:378-417 classifies every tagged run as kind osc, and refuses to create a printed URL across any OSC-tagged cells. terminal.js's provider order is OSC, printed web, printed file; an inert OSC target therefore does not fall through to a second provider for the same covered cells. terminal-links.js:153-158 allows validated OSC web activation to skip the printed-text predicate, but that call is reachable from oscLink only after oscTarget classified the target as web. Printed text instead passes isPlainWebUrl (:108-119), requiring an explicit http(s) prefix, no whitespace/control characters, and an absolute parsed http(s) URL with a host. openTerminalUrl (:69-75) performs no additional validation, so the adapter gate is load-bearing; the inspected call chain supplies it. The tunnel route (:128-158) retains its stricter predicate and cannot widen the accepted schemes.

Suggested bucket: highest/security if arbitrary local scheme execution were reachable; that route is refuted here. Could-be-highest: yes, this was a security-boundary candidate. Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation through the allowlist, inert fallback, provider precedence, and guarded opener caller above. possible_cover: none searched. event.summary: Lazy history validation promise is limited to retained rows
event.detail:
# Lazy history validation promise is limited to retained rows

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Checked whether the implementation specification falsely promises that every received history row is fully validated when queued history can be trimmed before decoding. Its promise explicitly concerns retained rows, matching the source; no separate documentation defect was established.

## Details

Assigned SPEC_impl.md The grid client says: "The existing sliced drain then validates each retained row in full before storing it; malformed content fails there even if nobody scrolls to it." This does not say evicted, unread rows must be semantically decoded. At the reviewed source, grid-model.js:331-370 checks each history-row envelope and copies the bounded row region; applyHistory (:875-913) queues the indexed message and calls trimQueue before a possible drain. The adjacent trimQueue contract explicitly drops unread rows that cannot remain under history_cap. drainHistory (:965-1008) calls walkBinaryRow for a row before copying its body, referenced links and identity token into the retained history. historyLine (:1095-1102) decodes only an already retained and validated row and caches no decoded tree. The source therefore supports the specification's retained-row qualifier and lazy-reader contract. This check was about the assigned documentation's replacement-model claim, not an independent runtime fuzz review.

Suggested bucket: other/documentation correctness if contradicted; no defect established. Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/loss-of-work route from discarded unread rows in this check. Confidence: confirmed by source and exact contract wording, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation and the exact retained-row qualifier quoted above. possible_cover: none; neighbour records were read as supplied interface context, not coverage sources. Caveat: this does not certify every malformed wire category or all history queue resource bounds. No runtime tests or reproductions were performed.
